title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1LC0RC_1LF0RD_1RA1LE_0LC---_1LD0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1LC0RC_1LF0RD_1RA1LE_0LC---_1LD0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. A counter with many digits: blocks (011)n separated by separators 1, 01, 111 that the sweeps rewrite like odometer digits. The lowest three levels are exactly periodic, with periods 8, 16 and 64 sweeps; the levels above have no period up to 4,096 sweeps. Lean proves four of the eight sweeps of the lowest level for every block length. No halt in 3.1·1016 steps (run-length accelerator).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 50,604 cells have been visited and 18,670 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.45×10<sup>14</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran with blocks of 6 cells, from blank tape for 3600 seconds and reached step 6.45×1014 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 99 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.169).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: D and A take turns crossing the blocks going right, turning each 011 into 100. A whole sweep from the left end, for every length of the first two blocks and any tape beyond: with an even first block and separator 1, the block gains one 011 and the separator becomes 01; with an odd first block and separator 01, the block gains two, the separator becomes 111 and the next block loses one. 1 D> 1 halts.

claims.title: The counter's low levels are periodic
claims.text: In the 21,693 sweeps of the first 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, level 1 (S1, n1, S2) is exactly periodic with period 8 from sweep 10, level 2 with period 16 from sweep 60, level 3 with period 64 from sweep 224; levels 4 to 6 have no period up to 4,096.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.1·10<sup>16</sup> steps (run-length accelerator)
claims.text: tools/c/rleaccel.cpp with blocks of 6 cells runs from blank tape to step 3.1·1016 without a halt; the tape is then 2.8·108 cells wide.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The low digits of the counter are regular; a proof would need a rule for what a carry does at every level, and the levels above the third show no regularity yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine counts: its tape is blocks of 011 between short separators that act like the digits of an odometer. The low digits turn over with perfect regularity, the high ones do not. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the run-length accelerator; 2.8·10<sup>8</sup> cells.
Exact periods, in sweeps, of the counter's three lowest levels.
of the lowest level's cycle of eight, proved for every block length.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is E reading 1. A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (bbtools.ctl) covers the run but still allows halts, with only a local constraint near the head: the head cell and the cells to its right read 111101. Nothing confines a halt to an edge.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.169).
After 109 steps the tape spans 50,604 cells (36,655 left of the start, 505 right), with a density of 1s of 0.369.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: An odometer of separators
html: Each sweep ends with the head extending the tape on the left in state D. Read from there, the tape is blocks a = 011 repeated, with short separators between them. At step 3·109:

Write it as a^n0 S1 a^n1 S2 a^n2 S3 a^n3 … and call (S1, n1, S2) level 1, (S3, n3, S4) level 2, and so on. The first block grows by one a per sweep. Level 1 runs through the same eight states forever (from sweep 10 on, checked to step 3·109):

7015111oddS1: 01 → 111, n1 − 1 (Lean)

Two sweeps in eight reach far into the tape: those are the carries. Level 2 is exactly periodic with period 16 sweeps (from sweep 60), level 3 with period 64 (from sweep 224), while n2 grows like n0/4, n4 stays at 21 and n6 grows like n0/16. From level 4 on no period up to 4,096 sweeps shows in the first 3·109 steps, and the block lengths there are irregular. A counter, regular in its low digits and chaotic in its high ones.

Lean (lean/Rules.lean) proves the sweeps marked in the table for every length of the blocks and every tape beyond them: sweep_1 (an even first block and separator 1) and sweep_01 (an odd first block and separator 01), with the rightward crossing walk_DA, in which D and A take turns over the blocks.

summary: Bouncer growing to the left over blocks of 011 with short separators that count like the digits of an odometer: the first three digits are exactly periodic (8, 16 and 64 sweeps), the higher ones irregular. Open.
family: bouncer with a multi-digit counter of 011 blocks, periodic low digits, chaotic high digits (F08)
